utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning. Please be seated. After some deliberations and before, and explicitly before we start today's hearing, the Trial Chamber feels it appropriate that we do not start this day, the day called the day of truth, that we spend some thoughts to this what might happen in the near future. This Tribunal is acting under Chapter 7 of the charter of the United Nations. In the past, we haven't seen any attempts to establish similar International Tribunals for the purpose of prosecuting persons responsible for serious violations of international humanitarian law committed in the territory of the Iraq. It's called the trial of truths. Let's hope that it will be also a day of the rule of law. Here in this Tribunal, we have seen, and we daily see it, what it means to become an innocent victim of a war. Therefore, I believe it is necessary to spend these thoughts also in the framework of this Tribunal established under Chapter 7 of the charter of the United Nations. One may ask what has this to do with the concrete cases in this Tribunal. It should be emphasised that the absence of justice in other areas does not justify not to grant justice in the area and the period of time we are mandated for. There is no equality in nonjustice. But first of all, being here always under the impression of the reports of those having survived the heinous crimes committed in former Yugoslavia, I think our thoughts should go for a moment to those innocent persons living now in Baghdad or elsewhere, having no chance to escape. Let us hope that there will be a last chance and let us hope that the harm for these innocent people will be as limited as possible. Let us hope that this will not undermine the law -- of the rule of law, not undermine public international law in general. Let us now call this concrete case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And the appearances, please for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. It's Joanna Korner, Nicholas Koumjian, and Ruth Karper, case manager, for the Prosecution. And we are pleased to see that Your Honour is at least majorly recovered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: For the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Branko Lukic and John Ostojic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. I have to announce that I got a message from Smash Bronovo, telling us to ICTY -- that's the stamp, it reads, "Smash Bronovo, to ICTY Trial Chamber II. Mr. S. Trifkovic, born the 19th of July, 1954, visited the first aid post of the general practitioners at Bronovo hospital today. In my opinion, a day or two of rest are necessary for him before he shall be able to testify before the Court. Smash Bronovo, Bronovolaan 5, 2597 AX, The Hague. Unreadable signature of doctor. 16th of March, 2003." So I think we have to accept that at least today, we will keep in contact with this expert whether he's able to testify tomorrow or the day after. I don't know. The Defence, do you have any better informations?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We contacted this morning, and we heard for the first time this morning that Mr. Trifkovic is sick. And we were promised that the Witness and Victims Unit will check on Dr. Trifkovic and on his health. So as you know, we cannot contact Dr. Trifkovic, and we also know only what you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the other remaining witness? When would it be possible for you to start with this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we probably need only one hour to tell the gentleman that he has to testify today, because we told him that he is going to testify tomorrow. So we can start today. We only have to transfer the message to him that he has to start today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would it be possible --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it should be necessary for us to see him. So probably we can start at 11.00. He should be a short witness, and I think that we might be able to finish with him today anyways even if we start at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: One can see with the watch that yesterday some repair works have been done. Would it be possible for you to separate yourselves that we can discuss in the meantime some administrative matters in Court? It would be really of assistance because a lot has to be done and to be said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this assistance. It might still be possible, and there is the likelihood that we can conclude the Defence case as scheduled, by the end of this week. But before we can come to this assessment, may I ask the Defence, is there anything new about any additional witness? Until now, we have this fact witness before us to be expected for today, and the estimate was, if I'm correct, one and a half hour of examination-in-chief. Then hopefully we can conclude the expert, conclude first the examination-in-chief. May I ask, what's your estimate -- what's the time you need for finalising this expert?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are we referring to Dr. Trifkovic, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Approximately a half hour to 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And then the Prosecution would need?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, certainly not less than three hours. There's quite a lot. Possibly a little more now. I originally estimated two to two and a half, but as a result of the examination-in-chief, the estimate has gone up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So in conclusion, it would mean that all in all, even worst-case thinking, within two days, this expert could be concluded.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, certainly, if he can start tomorrow, he'll be concluded on Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And then it would be as of Thursday the other expert for the Defence. And what is your updated estimate you would need for this?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Three to three and a half hours, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So it would also be possible to do this witness within two days, Thursday Friday, correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any other news about the other witnesses of the Defence suffering from some health problems or not found until now?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No additional news, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No additional news. So we could take it that for this week, there would be no additional witness from the side of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Therefore, we would only have to discuss some matters related to exhibits and other issues I've noted down. But then my view would immediately go to the left-hand side. For the next week, it is foreseen to start and hopefully to conclude the rebuttal. What is envisaged by the Prosecution for next week? What is planned, and when may we have a first overview of what is to be expected?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at the moment, anything we want to call in rebuttal, we would -- would be Rule 92 and one potential witness that we're awaiting. So whatever, it won't take a week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Following the rules, the order would be rebuttal, rejoinder, and then finally Chamber witnesses. You know that we have on the roll of Chamber witnesses hopefully two witnesses to come from Prijedor and one other maybe witness. This can only be determined following the 65 ter (i) conference the 31st of March, when in another Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. case, the time limit for an appeal has elapsed. Would the parties have any problems in case we learn that the two witnesses from Prijedor would be available next week, that we would in a slight change of the order of Rule 85, we would hear these witnesses during the period of rebuttal or, if this is not possible, during the week dedicated to rejoinder? First, the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it makes no difference to us, but I don't know whether my remarks about one of the witnesses you proposed to call were communicated to Your Honour, and Your Honour is still going to call him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: They were forwarded, and no doubt we are fully aware that this witness has been interviewed by the Prosecution as a suspect. A suspect in these rules not appearing as a judicial term, during trial. To be quite clear on this, I think the admonition in the beginning has to be the same as it was with witnesses Budimir and Travar. The only difference might be, and this would be a conclusion ad minorem, ad maiorem. But in case a witness that enjoys the right of an assignment of a counsel during the pre-trial stage, that the same right he would also enjoy during trial. So therefore, we are aware of these additional problems, but I think there is no hint at all in the moment that this witness would not testify to that -- at least to that end and this scope, he gave statements to the Prosecution. No doubt, he has a right to remain silent vis-a-vis those questions, and maybe even vis-a-vis certain areas where the questions tend to answers of a self-incriminatory nature. And as we stated already earlier, until now, it was seen by the Prosecution more or less only as a theoretical discrepancy, this Trial Chamber would not try to compel a witness, being a suspect from the point of view of the Prosecution, under Rule 90, para (E), to compel the witness to answer those questions. So therefore, it might be that in fact the one or other area could not be covered by this witness. But let us wait and see. Until now, we have no hints that the witness wants to make use of this right. But I take it from previous statements of the Prosecution that there is no obstacle that this Trial Chamber grants and has granted safe conduct and the same safe conduct for this witness, and the same would be true for the government of the Netherlands providing also safe conduct for this witness when being on the territory of the Netherlands.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Of course, if Your Honours and the Netherlands grant him safe conduct, that's a matter for Your Honours. And we certainly can't do anything about it. Your Honours may, perhaps, just want to consider the public perception of giving a man such as this safe conduct to come to this Tribunal and to sit in the witness box as a witness. But that's a matter for Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We are fully aware, and we also took this into account when discussing whether or not to summon this witness. It's not for the first time that I'm confronted with a similar problem, especially involved in white-collar crimes where you usually have always the safe haven where the even co-accused may disappear. And it's a balancing act whether it's in the interest of justice, whether it's in the interest of the accused to have a fair trial to hear these witnesses being suspect themselves. But as I take it, not indicted. And this would be for us, no doubt, a different assessment. But we take it that this witness has not been indicted by this Tribunal and not been indicted by any of the courts in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't know that. Your Honour, although strictly I ought not to be saying this because there are still sealed indictments, but the answer is he's not indicted at the moment, but we cannot possibly say whether he has been indicted by somebody else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Of course. And therefore, both are admonitions vis-a-vis Mr. Budimir and Mr. Travar already in the beginning, and also this restraint applying Rule 90, para (E), because we can't guarantee that testimony compelled in this way shall not be used as evidence in a subsequent prosecution against the witness for any offence other than false testimony. We are not able to safeguard that there is not such a prosecution in any other country in this world. So therefore, we don't want to make use of this paragraph (E) of Rule 90, but in case the witness feels fit and wants to make a testimony, even though being a suspect, then I think it's -- it might be even mandatory to hear this witness. I don't know, but hopefully we will learn in the near future, what about the other witness. There seem to be some difficulties --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, the driver? Yes, well, it's a matter for Your Honours if you want to hear from the driver. We have nothing to say about his driver.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We prefer to have our assessment always first after a witness has been heard. So hopefully, he will arrive. Then we have to discuss, and I think please correct me if I'm wrong, the statement of Madam Bozana Stakic that has arrived in a certified way. Are there any objections against the admission into evidence of this, my impression is unchanged, statement of Bozana Stakic?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if it's unchanged, no. We are trying to find it at the moment. I mean, if it's exactly the same, the answer is no, I'm told.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The only remarkable things that you can read under "additional remarks" since the statement was produced in English version, the letter was read out aloud back to the witness by the presiding officer. The witness stood by her statement. So can you finally let us know your position, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then this statement by Bozana Stakic is admitted into evidence pursuant to Rule 92 bis. I know it's a difficult question for the Defence already now when not knowing what will happen during rebuttal. What do you envisage to call during rejoinder?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We can only envision that we'll call witnesses to rebut that which they call in rebuttal, Your Honour. But until we know which witnesses, we obviously can't make that assessment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In the interest of the -- to have also in the near future as expeditious as possible trial, I think it could be helpful if the parties meet and discuss already now what would be the rebuttal witness or witnesses by the Prosecution in order that there might be an immediate reaction by the Defence. We all know how long it takes to call a witness. Then it would immediately follow, and I think the parties - let me know if I'm wrong - are still in agreement that once again, in deviation of that what is foreseen in the rules, we would, leaving aside deliberations, we would start with the oral final contributions by both parties, and only later then expecting the final brief. Is this still the opinion of the parties? And what about the real time estimate the parties would need in case we can follow this schedule for the final brief? Before giving you the floor, I want to emphasise that the Chamber will prepare a paper highlighting those factual and legal problems we would like to hear submissions by both parties especially, and this would be based an our ongoing deliberations both on legal and factual aspects of this case. No doubt that it is for the parties to give their additional remarks, comments, and whatever. It's foreseen under the rules. But in addition to this, we want to hear some comments on very special judicial and factual problems. Taking into account this, what would be the estimate the parties would need for the pre-trial brief in the moment scheduled for the Thursday before Easter? May I ask the Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry I'm not quite clear. Is Your Honour asking whether we want to put the delivery of not the pre-trial brief, but the closing brief? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Are you asking us whether we want more time or what? I'm not quite clear at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The first question is - we discussed this earlier - are you still in agreement that we start with the oral exchange of views, and then later have the closing briefs -- sorry, having then the closing briefs of this case? And then the question is: What is a real time estimate for the period of time you would need to prepare a well-elaborated and covering all issues closing final brief in this case?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, can I deal with the first question. Your Honour, it would not have been my personal choice to have dealt with matters in that order. However, I understand that Mr. Koumjian agreed to this, and because the Prosecution acts as one, I'm now not going to resile from that. Your Honour, then as far as we're concerned, we are content with the time allowed, which I think is the 17th of April or whatever, to put in our closing brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the point of view of the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The Defence is in agreement that we can proceed with the oral arguments and then submit the final brief, the written brief. However, we would like an additional seven to ten days on the written brief. And I'd also like to ask the Court if permitted, when would we be getting their factual and legal questions or paper as the Court has put it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This would follow as soon as possible and as soon as practicable, hopefully during this week. But no doubt, it might be that the following weekend will be needed for finalising this paper prepared by the Chamber. We'll take your remarks into consideration, and maybe there is a third way, to help you out, in case it would not be possible to finalise your final brief. It should, no doubt, be a final brief covering all these issues emanating from that what we have heard during the then 140 days in court covering all the exhibits. I know it's extremely difficult to do this. But I invite the parties really to concentrate on the core issues of the case, and primarily on the individual criminal responsibility of Dr. Stakic and refrain, please, from additional and overwhelming comments on circumstances not related to this, and especially this is true when it comes to questions of the history - let's put it this way - of area in both terms, in time and in space. So we can concentrate on this, we really can concentrate on the fourth amended indictment, I think it must be possible to have these briefs ready in April, hopefully before Easter, that we may come to a conclusion as soon as possible, that is, a final judgement. But may I hear from the Defence, is it to be expected that the accused in person tries either -- wants to testify, wants to make a statement as foreseen in the rules, or would it be necessary to make a reservation for a period of time when we would grant the last word to the accused in person?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with our last discussions with Dr. Stakic, we're still contemplating all the issues, and we haven't been able to concretely resolve any of them to this point. So I have no update for the Court. But we will attempt to meet with him either later this afternoon or tomorrow, and I'll get back to the Court as soon as possible on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. From this I take it that none of the options is yet excluded. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At this time, that is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then, next point, we are aware that there still is outstanding a 66 (C) decision. The Defence has the right to be put on notice that there has been such a 66 (C) in-camera meeting. A decision has not yet been handed down. May I now come to the question of exhibits. First, Madam Registrar, following your observations, you have laid down in a memo to those exhibits which have not yet been admitted or where there had been some problems. Has all these been resolved in the past? Could you please go through bullet by bullet your own remarks.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Okay. In regard to S11-1, the OTP is to provide a B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Has that happened?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Not yet, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we've got everything here. Perhaps rather than it being gone through handing documents in, we can deal with it after Court. It's here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The next one.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: S151A, the OTP to provide a new English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Not available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Not yet available.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yet.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: S365-1, the OTP to provide a final transcript of the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Available.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: S362, the final translation is expected.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Available.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: S368, the parties were to discuss about the additional file the Defence wants access to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I haven't heard from the Defence exactly what they want access to on that database, the electronic database.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, may we hear your comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's my understanding that we did at least discuss it with the Prosecution, but to the extent that my understanding from Mr. Lukic is incorrect, we'll get back to them on that issue this afternoon, S368.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. This remains open. The next one?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: S369, the translation into English is pending.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We have a summary, I'm told, Your Honour, not a full translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any objections by the parties, to have a summary only? Mr. Ostojic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: None that come to mind, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: S375, the translation into B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Being handed in now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: S393B, the original of the second page is expected. It's a handwritten page.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I thank you for this in fact readable side of the page. May we ask the Prosecution to try to produce a translation of what now can be clearly read on the back side of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's quite interesting. We checked, and I'm told by Ms. Karper that the CLSS said that it is not readable for the purposes of translation. But we'll have another go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Some words, no doubt, can be identified immediately. I don't know how to proceed in this case. Could the translation unit please be asked to translate these words which are without any doubt readable.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We can try, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We would appreciate it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But here, I don't think we need a colour copy. Then the next.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: S394, a colour copy was requested.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm told this was -- a colour copy was distributed on the 30th of January and admitted as S394-1B. We've extra copies if anybody wants them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This was a -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's the list of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Oh, yes. That's right. Then the next, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Then in relation to S404 and 405, the articles were to be provided in their entirety, the newspaper articles.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We have a blip on that one. We may have to get back to you on it. Apparently it's not on our list.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I think at one point the final article was found in the Internet version, but not in the newspaper version.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I see. I'm told, Your Honour, these came off the Internet, so it's just articles. I'm told - I'm just the mouthpiece for this one - we don't have anything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: To be quite clear about this, S404 and 405, Madam Registrar, do we have the entire article in English or in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: In English, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: From the point of view of the Defence, is there access through you for Dr. Stakic to the content of these documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At the moment we don't have it in front of us, Your Honour, but we'll stand on our previous objections if we made some on them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: What would be the next exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next two exhibits are Defence exhibits, D50, where the Defence was to provide an English translation based on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we hear some helpful comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure how much help I can assist the Court. But it was our understanding because the document was translated on the transcript, that that would be the official translation of D50. To the extent that was our error in interpretation, we'll from the transcript give the Court the specific translation of D50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think in case you yourself do not feel that it's necessary but make reference to the transcript, and this would be sufficient for you, you shouldn't have an additional burden.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: If the Prosecution agrees with this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then the next, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And finally regarding D55, some explanations were to be provided on the handwritten notes appearing on one of the copies and the different -- differences of final translation of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I would have to take a look at D55 again, Your Honour, and get back to you during the next break to give you a clear answer on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Then I believe there is only one final --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, before you move on, we've got -- Ms. Karper has given me a pile of stuff which is a number of revised translations. Well, first of all, we've got the constitution of Yugoslavia, which Your Honours requested on the 28th of February, the 1974. We've got a revised translation of S69 and S71 and S157. We've got a B/C/S translation of S370B; an English translation of S371; a better copy of S379; and a revised translation. S388, translation; 389, and so on. So, Your Honour, we've got -- there's the constitution. Your Honour, would it assist if we just hand out the other documents to your legal officer and the registry at the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think this would be helpful because we still have before us a lot of documents distributed, not yet tendered, by the Defence. I know there had been during the last week some discussions on this issue, but nevertheless I want to come back to this question. What is the intention of the Defence how to proceed, especially in order to avoid that precious courtroom time is wasted by the introduction of some of these documents during the testimony of especially experts. How do you want to proceed with your documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, we obviously will proceed in any manner the Court advises us to proceed. We thought we could introduce the documents in a similar fashion as the OTP introduced, but at that doesn't seem sometimes to be working in the manner in which I envisioned. So we can introduce it piecemeal, or as a whole, as a group, whatever way the Court suggests.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I already suggested, and I crosschecked the transcript, in November last year, that the most appropriate form would be that the parties come together and tell us which documents they agree they don't have any problems with. And then leave it for the Chamber to decide on the remaining documents. And I think this is still the less-time-consuming way of proceeding. If the Prosecution so agrees, we could proceed this way.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. I mean, what happened was that effectively, Dr. Trifkovic sat down, three binders of documents were produced, and in fact Dr. Trifkovic hasn't referred to a single document yet in three hours of evidence, although Mr. Lukic yesterday mentioned -- yesterday, Friday, a number of them. At the moment, I have no idea what's in half these documents, although looking at the list, the majority are newspaper articles. The ones that are actually referenced in his report, clearly there would be no objection to them going in. As to what the relevance of the other ones is, other than he looked at them, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You know that also related to the exhibits provided by Mr. Donia, on the one hand side, we limited the area both in time and space, but in principle, we admitted these documents where there was no objection by the Defence as SK documents. So there would be nothing against such a package solution, and then asking the Trial Chamber only to rule on those remaining documents where the parties can't agree on. Therefore, I invite the parties, when we have the break now and when -- whilst we are still on standby situation waiting for our witness, to go through these documents, and also together with Madam Registrar, give them provisional exhibit numbers, and then it would be admitted into evidence as a package save those where there is no agreement or where there is not yet an English translation. Can we agree to proceed this way?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it may be better to wait until the expert has completed his testimony. The thing about Dr. Donia was that he was taken through most of these documents in one -- the major ones. So we looked at them. I mean, at the moment, it's a tonne of newspaper articles which I absolutely confess I haven't read through because at the moment I'm not at all that clear that they are that relevant or anything. So I think it may perhaps be better to wait until the expert has completed his testimony. But obviously if we can agree with the Defence, we will. I noticed that in fact the 249 articles or books and articles were then reduced. We were given a separate list I think on Friday morning, a much shorter list of the exhibits that they wanted to put in. So it may be we'll be able to agree to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I can only invite the parties to proceed this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I would just like to say that I'm offended by counsel telling us that she doesn't think it's relevant because the articles relate to the time period much closer to the indictment than any of the articles or submissions that they gave into evidence. And I would just ask that they -- if they don't think it's relevant, it's the Court's decision to say if it's relevant. They don't want to put the whole picture on. We have argued that from day number one. They have had those articles not in November of 2002, they have had them well before and in fact in 1997 because we got the articles from the Prosecution. When we Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. submitted our exhibit list on the 18th of November, 2002, they did not, although I believe it's their duty --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. I don't think that we need to argue on these articles now. I think it's only to find out what can be accepted by both parties immediately for the admission into evidence, and then on the rest we will rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I can just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In the same spirit we did in the past.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Of course. And I appreciate that, Your Honour. But just, I have to make two short brief points on this. I think it will move it along a little faster. All the articles that we wanted, we were not advised that they were already translated by the OTP until several weeks ago, although on November 18th all they did to do was a crosscheck and the translation department certainly wouldn't have had to retranslate them. Secondly, if I may, with respect to all those documents, they are indeed in our opinion relevant and should be admitted. Unquestionably, they are relied upon by our expert. If we want, we will go through in each article and try in some fashion to get them introduced. It's incorrect that we reduced the list to a shorter group anticipating that the Court would reject the totality of those documents. We would request that a certain number of them be specifically introduced as a fallback theory. Our position is clear that we want all the articles in because we believe it fulfills the mandate of the Chamber to get as close to the truth as possible. However, if the Court rejects our request to admit them, we would like certain documents that Mr. Lukic highlighted on Friday, that those be introduced into evidence, but our position is that all them should be introduced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So finally, let's hear which articles and which documents are in dispute. Those that are not in dispute should have a provisional exhibit number, and then we are prepared to rule as soon as possible, maybe today, step by step only on the remaining documents. This will facilitate the admission into evidence procedure without wasting time, precious time of our expert. Any other issues to be raised by the parties? Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'd like to be heard on the Rule 66 motion before the Court delivers its opinion, if I may. I think it's Rule 66 (C) decision that the Court referenced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May I.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm not sure that Mr. Ostojic has a right to be heard. I have no particular objection, but it's supposed to be an ex parte motion for all its worth. I'm not sure what standing you have to be heard on it, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In the moment, I'm also eager to know what can be a submission by a party not being party of this procedure? But please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, I have two comments to make with respect to the submission. One is obviously the rule we disagree with, although it's the rule, and we will live with the rule as it's set forth, however it's my understanding that there were two submissions to the Court. One, the brief submission with respect to the document, and then the Court followed up and requested a complete group of those documents or statements. We object to the procedure. We object this Court without advising the defendant -- without advising the accused, without advising its counsel what the procedure is and the mechanism that goes on with respect to Rule 66 (C). I object to Rule 66 (C) and having ex parte conversations and sharing with the Court documents that, in the opinion of the Prosecution, may or may not lead so some credible evidence. Secondly, I most definitely object to there being a follow-up conversation and a submission, again without our knowledge, of documents given to the Court once the Court requested that. If the rule is clear that the OTP will submit a certain portion of the document, then that's where it should stand. If that changes, we believe our involvement should be included. If the Court is asking for additional information, then we should be advised of that; not to hear it through the grapevines, as we have. And we object to that procedure and we likewise object to Rule 66 (C) although I recognise the objection with respect to the rule is not the proper form here, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I don't know where your rumours stem from. 66 (C) clearly reads, "When making such an application, the Prosecution shall provide the Trial Chamber [but only the Trial Chamber] with the information that is sought to be kept confidential." And to make it quite clear, following the rationale of this Rule (C), it is for the Trial Chamber to defend the interest of the accused at the same time when the accused can't, for the reasons of Rule 66, be present during this explicitly foreseen in-camera meeting. And therefore, it is for this Trial Chamber to take the necessary steps that we have the necessary facts that we can decide on a secure basis. And there is nothing for a party not allowed to participate in these proceedings and to interfere.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may just comment quickly, Your Honour, and I understand that and we accept the Court's position. But it's a fact, it's not a rumour that the procedures as I have indicated occurred. So it's not a rumour, I just don't want to in open session identify quite frankly how that information came to the Defence, but I'd be glad to share with the Court if the Court wishes me to. But it's not a rumour, it's a fact that was shared with us by an officer of the court which we can clearly set forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's a fact that should never have been shared by an officer of the court. It's unfortunate that it was. The fact remains it's supposed to be a procedure which is ex parte. The only reason the Defence get any notice of it, and they should know nothing of what goes on, unless Your Honour rules that there should be disclosure, is because there was a ruling by Judge Hunt two years ago now in the Brdjanin case where we made such an application, and the Defence had to be notified that such an application had been made and that is it. Mr. Ostojic may not like the rule, but it is a rule, and his remedy is not at this stage of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It seems that they don't like the rule handed down by Judge Hunt that we have to be given notice of it. If that's the rule as the Court said in his opening remarks. Let's follow the rule. Let's follow them equally. We gladly accept the rules. My point is that the rules suggests the OTP is to give a statement if they want something that they think under the rules should be protected. If there is any further communication and requests by the Court for further documents, I think it takes it outside of Rule 66 (C), and the Defence should then be given another motion by the OTP suggesting that they are now amending or changing or altering their initial request to the Court. But the Defence should be notified of the circumstances surrounding that which involved the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I'm awfully sorry, but this Trial Chamber doesn't share your view. It's for the Trial Chamber to find out what is necessary to come a ruling under Rule 66 (C). No doubt, you have been sent notice that there will be such a ruling, and we will inform you when there has been such a ruling. Any other issues to be discussed? Then this Trial Chamber stays adjourned in any event until 11.00. If there should be a delay, we would announce it immediately to the parties. The trial stays adjourned until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: There was a request for closed session. Any objections by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we have the additional appearances, please. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the Prosecution, Nicholas Koumjian, Meline Arakelian and Ruth Karper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: There is a request also for pseudonym?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then it would be DI for this witness. The witness may be brought in, please. Closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The trial stays adjourned until tomorrow, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: at 12.53 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 18th day of March, 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 25
